new_scholarship.description: The Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship is the University of Rochester's premier undergraduate award, funded from a permanently endowed fund established in 2007 by Rich and Martha Handler with an ultimate commitment of $25 million, named in honour of Handler's parents. It is awarded to highly academically qualified first-year applicants with substantial levels of financial need, as demonstrated on their CSS Profile and FAFSA, who have overcome significant obstacles in their lives; scholars are selected on the basis of academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, and demonstrated mastery of complex challenges. Scholars receive assured, complete financial support - tuition, fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation - for the duration of the regular four-year academic program, with health insurance covered if applicable, plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000.
new_scholarship.best_fit: A first-year, fall-term applicant, domestic or international, with strong results in challenging coursework, high demonstrated financial need, a record of overcoming significant obstacles, and demonstrable leadership potential, who can secure a nomination from a non-related counselor, teacher or community organization official, can file the required financial aid documents, and can attend the mandatory two-part virtual finalist interview in mid-February.
new_scholarship.funding_period: One-time enrichment fund of up to $5,000 over the course of a four-year experience
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to first-year, fall-term domestic and international applicants; transfer and spring applicants are not eligible. Candidates must show demonstrated academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, resiliency in the face of complex challenges, and high financial need documented on the CSS Profile and FAFSA. A high school or independent counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official must nominate the student between 15 September and 30 November; nominations from students or parents are not accepted and the nominator must not be related to the student. All first-year applicants are reviewed for the scholarship simply by submitting an application and completing the necessary financial aid documents, with no additional materials required. International students are eligible and are selected each year.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: Not published on the Handler Scholarship page. It is set by University of Rochester undergraduate admission: international applicants must submit Duolingo English Test, IELTS or TOEFL iBT results, or an English Proficiency Waiver Request, by their application deadline. Recommended scores are Duolingo 130, IELTS 7.5, and TOEFL iBT 100 (former scoring) or 5 (new scoring).
new_scholarship.selection_notes: All University of Rochester first-year applicants are reviewed for the Handler Scholarship simply by submitting an application and completing the necessary financial aid documents, with no additional materials required; a nomination by an eligible third party is what places a candidate in the competition. Selection is made on the basis of academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, and demonstrated mastery of complex challenges, together with substantial demonstrated financial need on the CSS Profile and FAFSA. No published weighting exists across the criteria. Finalists are notified by email in mid-February and must attend a mandatory two-part virtual interview event; non-selected finalists remain eligible for other competitive high-value and merit scholarships. Nominating a student does not guarantee acceptance or receipt of the award, and a student is eligible to receive only one merit scholarship from the University of Rochester.
new_scholarship.notes: Award name: the page heading and browser title use 'Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship'; the body text and the University's financial aid Scholarships page also use 'Alan and Jane Handler Scholarship'. Funding amount: the University publishes no single total dollar value for the award, which is defined as the cost of attendance. The only published dollar figures are the enrichment fund of up to $5,000 (recorded as funding_amount) and the Academic Supply grant of $100 per year; the cost of attendance itself is published separately (2026-27: $96,022 residential, $87,080 off-campus, $81,364 with parents) and has not been presented as the Handler award value. Deadline date: the Handler page states 'December 1' without a year; the Handler nomination form lists entrance term 'Fall 2027' and the financial aid pages publish fall 2027 deadlines, so the operative date for the current cycle is 1 December 2026. English scores are published by the University as recommended, not minimum, scores. Unverified or not published: no monthly stipend, no total award value, no application fee on the scholarship page, no Handler-specific image asset, and no Handler-specific English-language requirement.

The third-party nomination - the route into the competition - opens 15 September and closes 30 November, and the University states it does not accept nominations from students or parents. The applicant's own application 'does not have to be submitted as Early Decision, but should be submitted by December 1', which the Dates and Deadlines page identifies as the priority scholarship deadline for highest scholarship consideration; Regular Decision continues to 5 January. The Handler page states 'December 1' without a year; the Handler nomination form lists entrance term 'Fall 2027' and the financial aid pages publish fall 2027 deadlines, so the operative date for the current cycle is 1 December 2026. Separately, award holders must apply for financial aid annually by 15 March for full consideration.

programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: 'A four-year scholarship to the University of Rochester in the amount of the cost of attendance. Health insurance is covered if applicable.' Also: 'The Handler Scholarship (combined with any federal and state grants/scholarships) will cover your tuition and mandatory fees for up to eight semesters or until your first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first.' The University describes the award as 'more-than-full-tuition'. Recorded as fully funded because every cost-of-attendance head is covered. The items the University explicitly does not cover sit outside the cost of attendance or are penalties and discretionary spend: Rocky Bucks/Flex Account funds; individual fees not required for a course such as dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and Dean's fees; off-campus housing costs above the standard allowance; and any cost incurred while not enrolled at the University of Rochester. Unused book grants are not refundable and may not be used for other expenses. Need-based aid is recalculated annually, so the package may change between years.

programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Explicit. The Handler Scholarship FAQ states: 'Yes, our Handler Scholars are representative of the overall class, thus international students will be selected each year.' The International Students admissions page states the University 'is committed to meeting the full demonstrated need of all admitted students regardless of citizenship'. Two official qualifications apply: financial need is a contributing factor for international applicants so admission is highly selective for students with financial need, and 'due to limited resources, only a small number of international applicants will qualify for need-based financial aid from the University'. International students submit the CSS Profile and do not complete the FAFSA.

The International Students admissions page states all international students must submit proof of English proficiency by exam or by an English Proficiency Waiver Request by their application deadline, and publishes recommended - not minimum - scores of Duolingo 130, IELTS 7.5 and TOEFL iBT 100 (former scoring) or 5 (new scoring), noting that applicants whose scores fall outside those ranges are still encouraged to apply. Applicants may instead request a waiver as native English speakers, after at least three years of high school where English was the primary language of instruction, or as transfer applicants with a year or more of US college-level coursework.

programme_detail_official.description: The Alan and Jane Handler Endowed Scholarship is the University of Rochester's premier award, funded from a permanently endowed fund created in 2007 by Rich and Martha Handler with an ultimate commitment of $25 million. Handler Scholars receive assured, complete financial support - tuition, fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation - for the duration of the regular four-year academic program, with health insurance covered if applicable, plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000. Selection is based on academic excellence, outstanding potential to be future leaders, demonstrated mastery of complex challenges, and substantial financial need shown on the CSS Profile and FAFSA, and international students are selected each year.
programme_detail_official.program_type: University premier full-need undergraduate scholarship (institutional, nomination-based)
programme_detail_official.region: United States (University of Rochester, New York)
programme_detail_official.coverage: Complete financial support for the duration of the regular four-year academic program: tuition and mandatory fees (combined with any federal and state grants/scholarships) for up to eight semesters or until the first bachelor's degree requirements are met; on-campus housing and food based on housing and meal plan selection, or a standard off-campus allowance covering rent, utilities, groceries and transportation to campus; books through a $100-per-year Academic Supply grant; annual personal and transportation allowances inside the cost of attendance; and health insurance if applicable. Plus an enrichment fund of up to $5,000. Not covered: Rocky Bucks/Flex Account funds; individual fees not required for a course such as dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and Dean's fees; off-campus housing costs above the standard allowance; and any cost incurred while not enrolled at the University of Rochester.

application_readiness_checklist: Ask a high school or independent counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official who is not a relative to nominate you between 15 September and 30 November; you and your parents cannot nominate yourself
Confirm your nominator received a submission confirmation, and that you received the next-steps email - all nominated students are emailed their next steps

Submit the University of Rochester first-year application through the Common Application or Coalition for College Application by 1 December, treating that as the operative deadline rather than the 5 January Regular Decision date
File the CSS Profile to school code 2928 and, if you are a domestic applicant, the FAFSA to school code 002894; international applicants file the CSS Profile only

If you are an international applicant not seeking need-based aid, complete the International Financial Support Form instead of the CSS Profile, plus a sponsor letter if your funding source is not listed on the form
Register for and submit English proficiency exam results, or file an English Proficiency Waiver Request, by your application deadline if you are an international applicant
Have your school send the secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and the school report / counselor recommendation directly through the application platform, not by email
Write the required 250-word University of Rochester supplemental essay for the current cycle
Clear mid-February for the mandatory two-part virtual finalist interview, and raise any extenuating circumstances as early as possible
Diarise 15 March for the annual financial aid reapplication that renewal requires
common_rejection_risks: No nomination at all - it is the entry ticket to the competition and cannot be supplied by the student or a parent
A nomination from a relative, which the University states is not permitted
Weak demonstrated financial need, because substantial need on the CSS Profile and FAFSA is an explicit criterion and not a tie-breaker
Assuming a nomination guarantees acceptance or the award - the University says it guarantees neither
Missing or declining the mandatory mid-February finalist interview
Applying as a transfer or spring applicant, who are not eligible
Aiming at the 5 January Regular Decision deadline and losing priority scholarship consideration
Submitting the admissions application without completing the financial aid documents, which the University requires for the review
For international applicants, assuming a FAFSA is required, or assuming need-based aid is broadly available - only a small number of international applicants qualify
Failing to maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress or missing the 15 March annual aid reapplication, which breaks renewal
estimated_uncovered_costs: Rocky Bucks / Flex Account spending on campus dining, non-food items such as laundry, printing and copying, and several off-campus restaurants and stores
Individual fees not required for a course: dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges and Dean's fees
Off-campus housing and living costs above the standard allowance, which the student must cover
Trips home and personal expenses beyond the annual transportation and personal-expense allowance, which the University notes may not cover every personal expense or trip home
Any cost incurred while not enrolled at the University of Rochester, or toward another institution
Costs beyond eight semesters if the degree takes longer than the regular four-year program

research_notes.logo: Probed the official University of Rochester wordmark on the awarding body's own domain. The Handler Scholarship page (admissions.rochester.edu/handler-scholarship) renders the site header logo from https://admissions.rochester.edu/wp-content/themes/ur-core/img/theme/branding-assets/new-logo.svg, an admissions.rochester.edu theme branding asset served by the same registrable domain as the official source page. A live HEAD request returned HTTP 200 with content-type image/svg+xml and content-length 21909 bytes. The SVG body was inspected: the mark is drawn in fill #001E5F (navy) on white background rects, so it is a dark-on-light wordmark and not the excluded white-on-transparent variant. This asset is already registered in backend/config/official_logo_overrides.json under the host 'admissions.rochester.edu', so the URL is consistent with the existing verified entry. The alternative asset at https://www.rochester.edu/assets/images/brand/logos/primary_horizontal_knockout.svg was probed and returned HTTP 200 with image/svg+xml, but its filename and role make it a white 'knockout' wordmark, which PART D rule 6 deliberately excludes, so it was not used. The Technolutions CDN host at admissions-enrollment-rochester-edu.cdn.technolutions.net was also rejected as a third-party host. No Handler-specific logo asset is published.
unverified: No single total dollar award value is published; the University defines the award as the cost of attendance and publishes those cost figures separately, so no total has been computed
No monthly stipend amount is published; living support is delivered as annual cost-of-attendance allowances
The admissions application fee is not stated on the scholarship page
Any cap on the number of nominations one nominator may submit in a cycle is not published
No certified-translation requirement for non-English documents is published on the pages read
No Handler-specific English-language requirement is published; the recorded scores are the admissions requirement for international applicants
No Handler-specific image asset is published

The University states the application 'should' be submitted by 1 December rather than a hard cut-off; the 1 December date is the priority scholarship deadline, and Regular Decision continues to 5 January with lower scholarship priority
research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The Handler Scholarship page describes 'a four-year scholarship to the University of Rochester' whose coverage runs 'for up to eight semesters or until your first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first', and the ideal-candidate list is limited to 'first-year, fall term domestic and international applicants'. The award therefore funds a first bachelor's degree at undergraduate level, so degree_levels is Bachelor's. Only first-year entry is funded - transfer and spring applicants are explicitly not eligible - and no master's coverage is described.
